input.note: instant == edge (tape-loading.md TAPE-INSTANT-EQUIV-001): a short DATA block (flag 0xFF) is loaded BOTH by the instant/trap loader (no ROM, no pulses, tStates 0) AND by the real ROM LD-BYTES edge-load (0x0556) over the W10.9 pulse stream; the two must agree on the observable result {ok, bytesLoaded, RAM} and both equal the source bytes. Same 24-byte data as TAPE-EDGE-LOAD-001 so the parallel is exact. The edge half is ~7.5M T; budget 12,000,000 bounds it. Fabrication-free: expected.ram IS the source bytes.

instant == edge for a HEADER flag (0x00 < 0x80 -> the 8063-pilot leader on the edge half), exercising the pilot-by-flag path of the real ROM against the flag-independent instant trap. 8 source data bytes -> body [0x00, ...data, checksum]. The edge half is ~17.6M T; budget 25,000,000.

VERIFY (load: false, TAPE-INSTANT-VERIFY-001) against RAM already holding the same 8 bytes: the real ROM compares every byte, stores nothing, and succeeds. Expected recorded from the real ROM edge load (the runner re-checks edge == expected).

VERIFY against RAM that differs at byte 3 (0xEE instead of 0x43): the real ROM stops at the first difference with carry reset and bytesLoaded = 3 (DE decremented once per verified byte), storing nothing. The pre-2026-11 instantLoad ignored VERIFY and returned ok.

A block shorter than DE (TAPE-INSTANT-SHORT-001): 4 data bytes + checksum 0xBF, DE = 8. The real ROM stores all 5 bytes after the flag (the checksum byte as data), then times out: carry reset, bytesLoaded 5. The pre-2026-11 instantLoad stored 4 and could report success.
A block longer than DE: 8 data bytes, DE = 4. The real ROM stores 4 bytes, reads the 5th data byte as the checksum (parity fails) and stops: carry reset, bytesLoaded 4.

A load at IX = 0x3FFE on a machine with a write-protected ROM (MACHINE-ROM-READONLY-001): the two bytes that land in ROM are dropped (0x3FFE/0x3FFF keep the ROM bytes 42 3C), the two in RAM are stored, and the load succeeds — on both the real-ROM edge load and the instant loader.
